jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Experimental Particle Physics
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Fellow in Experimental Particle Physics at the University of Michigan
 
The experimental particle physics group at the University of Michigan invites applications for a postdoctoral fellow position to work on the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and on R&D for a future electron-positron Higgs factory. The Michigan ATLAS team is actively engaged in the operation, maintenance, and upgrade of the ATLAS muon detector, along with its performance studies. Our group also leads a broad physics program at the LHC, with emphasis on electroweak physics, Higgs boson studies, and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. Recently, we have launched several major detector R&D initiatives, including the development of a straw tracker and muon detector for the proposed Higgs factory.
 
The successful candidate has the option to be based in Ann Arbor, Michigan (US) or at CERN (Switzerland), and will work closely with group members to support our ATLAS muon detector commitments, lead major physics analysis--particularly those targeting rare Higgs boson decays and Higgs boson pair production--and contribute to R&D for FCC-ee. Interested applicants should submit their curriculum vitae and a statement of research to umatlas-postdoc-search@umich.edu, and arrange for three letters of reference to be sent, preferably before January 31, 2026. Review of applications will begin as soon as they are complete. Preference will be given to candidates with strong experience in machine learning. A PhD in experimental particle physics is required.
 
The initial appointment is for one year, renewable annually for up to five years, contingent on performance and funding availability.

Legal Information
The University of Michigan conducts background checks on all job candidates upon acceptance of a contingent offer and may use a third-party administrator for this process. Background checks are performed in compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act. If based in Ann Arbor, the candidate must be eligible for employment in the United States at the time of the start date. Continued employment is contingent on maintaining valid immigration status. The University of Michigan is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral position in charm-baryon physics with the Belle II experiment
jobs.description:
General information:
Workplace: Marseille, France
Type of contract: CDD contract
Contract period: 2 years
Expected date of employment: between February 1st and April 1st 2026
Renumeration: 3081...4291 EUR per month, depending on the experience
Desired level of education: PhD
Deadline for application: 17/December/2025
Apply through: https://emploi.cnrs.fr/Offres/CDD/UMR7346-ANNPOR-171/Default.aspx?lang=EN

Project description:
Decays of heavy-quark hadrons allow to perform indirect searches for effects beyond the Standard Model, by comparing the measured decay properties to their Standard Model predictions. Although our world is made of baryons, most such studies in heavy-flavour physics to date are performed with mesons, and our knowledge of heavy-quark baryon properties remains very limited. 
Although the baryons that contain a charm quark and at least one strange quark have been studied for more than 40 years, there are still significant gaps in our knowledge of their properties and decays. Notably, the absolute branching fractions of the Xi_c baryon decays are known to a very limited precision, while for the Omega_c, only relative decay rates have been measured. This is a significant limitation for any searches for physics beyond the Standard Model involving charm-baryon decays, or beauty baryons decays into charm baryons. 

The Belle II detector at KEK (Japan) is aimed at precision measurements of properties of beauty and charm hadrons, as well as tau leptons (https://inspirehep.net/literature/1692393). The Belle II collaboration consists of more than 1000 scientists and is taking data since 2019. The key feature of the Belle II detector is the nearly 4pi angular acceptance, which allows to perform the full reconstruction of the visible collision products and calculation of the missing energy. Combined with conservation laws in e+e-->ccbar process (baryon number, electric charge, quark flavours), this allows to fully reconstruct only one charm hadron and deduce the properties of the other one. This, together with the powerful algorithms for full event interpretation and B-tagging, opens several opportunities to improve our knowledge of the strange-charm-baryon decay rates. The techniques for inclusive reconstruction of charm baryons developed in https://inspirehep.net/literature/1275621 will be extended to strange-charm baryons and improved during this project. This technique can then be extended to other measurements, such as semileptonic decays of charm baryons.

Activities:
Data analysis, participation to the Belle II data taking and detector operation, outreach and dissemination, student supervision. 

Work context:
The successful candidate will be based at CPPM, Marseille (https://www.cppm.in2p3.fr). Travels to KEK (Japan) for collaboration meetings, and longer stays for participation to the data taking, are foreseen. The funding for this position comes from the ANR grant StrangeCharm.

Located in the heart of the Parc National des Calanques, on the Luminy campus, the CPPM is a joint research laboratory of the CNRS and Aix-Marseille University, with around 180 researchers, engineers and PhD students. The laboratory studies subjects ranging from particle physics to astroparticle physics and cosmology, with a strong technological focus on electronics, mechanics, instrumentation and computing, enabling the design and construction of cutting-edge detection systems, often called upon to operate under extreme conditions: in the depths of the sea, in space or underground. Most of our research is carried out as part of leading international scientific collaborations, and our contributions are recognized worldwide. CPPM is committed to ethical research and promotes diversity and inclusion in the workplace, and provides administrative and logistical support to newcomers, particularly PhD students.

Skills:
PhD in experimental particle physics.
Excellent skills in data analysis and software (python, ROOT, C++), teamwork abilities and proficiency in English.
Experience in Belle II data analysis is appreciated but not mandatory.

Additional information:
Interested researchers are invited to submit their application that includes: a motivation letter, curriculum vitae, list of publications and a copy of their latest university degree. The applications must be submitted through the CNRS web portal https://emploi.cnrs.fr/Offres/CDD/UMR7346-ANNPOR-171/Default.aspx?lang=EN. Three letters of recommendation are requested as a part of this procedure. 

For more information, contact Vitalii Lisovskyi (lisovskyi@cppm.in2p3.fr)

Further references:
https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7826 
https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.09738
https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12093

jobs.title: PhD student position in experimental astroparticle physics
jobs.description:
The Laboratory of Cosmic Particles (LCP) of EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, invites applications for a PhD student position in experimental astroparticle physics. 

The successful candidate will join the DAMPE and HERD international collaborations, dedicated to high-energy cosmic-ray and gamma-ray observations from space.

The main focus of the PhD project will be Monte Carlo simulations for HERD, used to model particle interactions in the detector and to estimate the expected electron + positron flux. The work will involve developing the analysis framework for the HERD data expected from 2028, and the candidate will later take a leading role in their analysis once the data become available. Depending on the candidate’s interests, there will also be opportunities to contribute to the development and testing of scintillating-fibre tracking detectors for space applications.

The position, which includes teaching duties at the Bachelor’s or Master’s level, will start at the earliest convenient date for the selected candidate, and preferably no later than March 1, 2026.

The selected PhD student will be required to enrol in the Physics program (EDPY) of the EPFL Doctoral School, and employment is offered for a total duration of up to four years. Information on the doctoral school and employment conditions at EPFL can be found online [1–3]. Applicants are expected to hold a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Physics at the start of employment. The ideal candidate is strongly motivated for fundamental research and has a solid background in particle physics. Experience in data analysis, detector simulations, and scientific programming is an asset.

Candidates should submit a single PDF file containing the following documents, in the order listed below:
  1. A motivation letter,
  2. A curriculum vitae,
  3. The names and email addresses of two referees who have agreed to provide reference letters,
  4. A transcript of grades for both the Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees.
The compiled PDF should be sent to Prof. Chiara Perrina at Chiara.Perrina@epfl.ch by December 2, 2025.

Applicants are encouraged to inform their referees in advance so that the referees can send their letters to Prof. Chiara Perrina at Chiara.Perrina@epfl.ch by December 2, 2025.

jobs.title: Ph.D. Positions in Dark Matter & Neutrino Experiments
jobs.description:
The particle astrophysics and underground physics program at the School of Science, Westlake University (Hangzhou, China), led by Prof. Shengchao Li, is inviting international applications for one to two fully-funded Ph.D. positions in experimental dark matter and neutrino physics.

About Our Research
Our group works at the frontier of low-background rare-event detection, with a strong focus on:
  • Dark matter direct detection, including liquid xenon detector technology, in the XENONnT and XLZD experiments
  • Solar and reactor neutrino measurements, with an emphasis on sub-MeV physics and calibration strategies, in the RELICS experiment
  • Detector R&D, covering cryogenic systems, photon-sensor development, calibration source design, and low-energy signal modeling
  • Data analysis & simulation, including background characterization, noble-element simulation (NEST), signal reconstruction, and advanced statistical/ML methods
Our current projects include liquid-xenon calibration studies, xenon/argon detector R&D, and the development of next-generation large-scale detectors in collaboration with domestic and international partners.
More information on the School of Science website:
https://physics.westlake.edu.cn/en/
More information about our research can be found at: https://scli.lab.westlake.edu.cn/

Candidate Profile
We welcome highly motivated students with strong academic preparation in:
  • Experimental particle physics, nuclear physics, or related fields
  • Detector physics, data analysis
  • Electronic and/or cryogenic instrumentation
  • Programming and statistical analysis (Python/C++/ML methods)
  • Good communication skills in English and an interest in collaborative research
Prior experience in dark matter or neutrino experiments is beneficial but not required.

Research Environment
Our group is embedded in Westlake’s rapidly expanding program in particle and astroparticle physics. We maintain active collaborations with groups in China and abroad, and students will have opportunities to participate in large-scale experiments as well as in-house detector development. The team currently includes multiple postdoctoral researchers and graduate students, providing a supportive and interactive research atmosphere.

Application Procedure
All applicants should apply for the Ph.D. Program in Physics at Westlake University.

Detailed guidelines:

Prof. Shengchao Li: lishengchao@westlake.edu.cn
School of Science Admissions: admission_science@westlake.edu.cn

Visiting students:
We also offer visiting scholar positions for undergraduate students in their junior and senior years, for a period of more than three months.

About Westlake University
Westlake University is a young, research-driven institution dedicated to excellence in fundamental science and cutting-edge technology. With strong public and private support, it provides an international research environment, modern facilities, and a commitment to maintaining a streamlined structure to ensure high-quality training for graduate students.

jobs.title: Full Professor (W2, Tenure Track W2) in Experimental Astroparticle Physics
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences at RWTH Aachen University invites applications for a Full Professorship (W2, Tenure Track W2) in Experimental Astroparticle Physics. This is a tenure-track professorship for a five-year term leading to a tenured W2 position. The position is funded by the Tenure Track Program of the German federal and state governments. This call for applications is therefore particularly targeted at early career researchers. For further information about the tenure track process, please visit www.rwth-aachen.de/tenuretrack.

Profile of the professorship
We are inviting applications for the position of full professor in the area of experimental astroparticle physics, to be filled as soon as possible. The applicant carries out experimental research in the field of astroparticle physics, broadly defined. He/she has achieved international visibility through publications in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals. The research may focus on the development of detectors or data analysis in one or more of the following areas: cosmic rays, gamma rays, neutrinos, dark matter, axions, gravitational waves. She/he will be interested in developing synergies with existing RWTH activities in particle and astroparticle physics and beyond. The professorship will be tenured after successful evaluation. The future professor is expected to raise external funds, to contribute to the strategic development of the department and to teach experimental physics at the bachelor’s and master’s level.

Your qualifications
The requirements include a doctoral degree and additional research experience, such as a habilitation (post-doctoral lecturing qualification) or equivalent achievements gained as a university researcher or professor or in a research position outside academia. Teaching ability and dedication are essential and the application should include proof of this. Fluent German is not required to start the position but the successful candidate will be expected to hold classes in German within the first 5 years. Participation in academic self-administration is expected.

Attractive environment
RWTH Aachen University is one of Germany's pre-eminent Universities of Excellence and is renowned for its high-quality teaching and world-class research. Assuming profound responsibility towards society, RWTH addresses bold scientific questions and translates its knowledge into meaningful applications. RWTH strives for the convergence of knowledge, methods, and findings and integrates in-depth disciplinary knowledge within the interdisciplinary research consortia established in its eight profile areas. The University's dynamic, creative, and international environment encompasses efficient research networks and institutionalized collaborations. With its innovative RWTH Aachen Campus project, the University boasts one of the largest technology-oriented research environments in Europe.

Your application
The official job description can be found at https://www.rwth-aachen.de/jobs/professors. Please submit your application online by January 14, 2026 through the RWTH appointment portal at: www.berufungsportal.rwth-aachen.de. For inquiries specific to the academic position, please reach out to Prof. Dr. Philipp Mertsch (contact details below). If you encounter technical issues with the appointment portal, please get in touch with our support team (contact details below).

This position is available on a part-time basis upon request. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender. RWTH Aachen University is recognized as a familyfriendly institution and provides a dual career program to support partner hiring. Our Family Services Center, part of the Equal Opportunities Office, is available to offer guidance on family matters, including childcare and caregiving responsibilities. At RWTH Aachen University, we are dedicated to advancing women’s careers and strongly encourage women to apply. When candidates have equal qualifications, skills, and accomplishments, preference may be given to women, provided there are no overriding considerations in favor of another candidate. We also welcome applications from qualified individuals with disabilities and those with equivalent status, and we look forward to applications from international candidates. jobs.title: Postdoctoral position in experimental particle physics
jobs.description:
The Prof. Ostrovskiy's group at the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) is continuously looking for active, self-motivated postdoctoral researchers with background in high-energy, astroparticle, or nuclear physics.

The group is playing a leading role in the searches for magnetic monopoles in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC with the MoEDAL experiment and participates in searches for other exotics in p-p collisions. The group is also involved in the installation and commissioning of the MoEDAL’s Apparatus for Penetrating Particles (MAPP) that will search for long-lived and milli-charged particles. The group members are involved in the simulations, analysis, and installation activities, as well as serving in leadership roles in the MoEDAL/MAPP collaboration.

The successful candidate will be expected to take charge of one or several of the above activities. Experience with Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations and data analysis using ROOT and Python is required.

Candidates will need to have completed their Ph.D. in Physics or a related field at the start of appointment.

The position comes with attractive starting salary and anticipated further increases based on annual review performance. Opportunities exist to apply for competitive fellowships and extra funds from the CAS/IHEP during the appointment. Outstanding postdocs may eventually be promoted to a tenure-track faculty position at IHEP. The position is initially for two years, with potential extensions for 2-4 more years.

Applicants should send their CV and a statement of purpose (explaining your scientific goals and how your qualifications will allow you to achieve them) to Prof. Igor Ostrovskiy (igor.ostrovskiy@ihep.ac.cn). Please also provide the names and contact information of three references who will supply letters of recommendation upon request.

Review of the applications will begin immediately and continue until the positions are filled. Email Prof. Igor Ostrovskiy with any questions.

jobs.description:

It provides unique opportunities for self-directed research in experimental physics through work on the Fermilab particle physics experiment of the candidate's choice. 

The Fermilab experimental program includes collider and cosmic physics, studies of neutrinos, muons, and research at the intersection of high energy physics and quantum information science, as well as R&D and planning for future experiments. This year we are particularly interested in applications focused on neutrino, muon and collider physics. 

As an organization, Fermilab is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining talent and cultivating a work environment that supports scientific, technological, and operational excellence. Fermilab and the Wilson Fellowship Committee value candidates who show potential for growth and scientific leadership. Candidates from outside particle physics or with non-traditional career paths are encouraged to apply. Successful candidates are expected to respect and value individual differences. 

The appointment is for an initial term of three (3) years with the possibility for renewal for an additional three (3) years upon completion of a successful review after the first two (2) years; thereafter, the potential exists for eventual appointment without term limit.

jobs.title: Post-doctoral position
jobs.description:
The position at the Experimental Nuclear and Particle Physics Center lasts for 12 months and can be extended for a longer period.
 
Vilnius University (VU) is one of the oldest higher education institutions in Eastern and Central Europe. It tops the ranking as the number one university in Lithuania and leads the country in education, a broad spectrum of fundamental and applied research, training and retraining programs, and consultancy services and provides research and development services to a wide range of businesses. VU offers dynamic research and training environment and is well integrated into a collaborative network of international universities.
 
VU Faculty of Physics research teams contribute to experimental particle physics research at the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The applied physicists are also involved in DRD3, DRD6 and DRD7 Collaborations. The experimental data analysis group performs the CMS data analysis, contributes to both the CMS Tracker Phase II upgrade and the central M&O activities. The CMS data analysis focuses on a precise differential cross-section measurement of the quark-antiquark annihilation reaction with the emergence of a charged lepton-antilepton pair (the Drell-Yan process) in a wide range of the two-lepton invariance mass. The wire-bonding and testing site for the Tracker extension pixel modules (TEPX) is set-up by the Experimental Nuclear and Particle Physics Center.
 
The candidate will contribute to the TEPX testing site activities, perform the CMS data analysis (Drell-Yan, HH, or Majorana neutrinos), participate in CMS collaboration EPR tasks, and contribute to experimental particle physics lectures. Student supervision might be requested. Both staying in Lithuania and visits to CERN are expected.
 
Requirements
-         A PhD degree in experimental particle physics.
-         Good written and spoken English.
-         Experience with large-scale data analysis, good knowledge of electronics, and hands-on experience in a scientific lab will be considered an advantage.
-         A candidate is expected to work on-site in Vilnius University Saulėtekis Campus at least for a half of the contract duration.
 
We offer

-         Gross salary (before taxes) of min. 2500 EUR/month.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in experimental nuclear physics
jobs.description:
The Department of Physics & Astronomy at Stony Brook University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in experimental nuclear physics. Candidates from all areas of experimental nuclear and particle physics are encouraged to apply. The successful applicant is expected to develop an independent research program in nuclear physics with creativity and vision.

Researchers interested in contributing to Stony Brook’s long-term vision surrounding the realization of the Electron Ion Collider (EIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) are particularly encouraged to apply. The appointed faculty will join Stony Brook’s experimental nuclear physics group and the Center for Frontiers in Nuclear Science, engaged in a dynamic research program focused on strongly interacting QCD matter, hadron structure and its formation, and precision tests of the Standard Model.

Stony Brook’s group plays leading roles in EIC science development, advanced EIC detector (ePIC) instrumentation development and simulations, and is deeply involved in international collaborations—including sPHENIX (RHIC), MOLLER and others at Jefferson Lab, MUSE at PSI, ARIEL at TRIUMF, and the IceCube experiment. The group collaborates closely with the Center for Nuclear Theory (CNT), the Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics (YITP) at Stony Brook and maintains strong ties with BNL’s experimental and theoretical physics groups.

jobs.title: Research Associate in Experimental Physics
jobs.description:
The Institute of Physics is looking for a Research Associate in Experimental Physics

Would you like to work at the interface between particle physics and data science by applying and developing machine learning (ML) algorithms and software tools? Then, this project will give you the opportunity to take a leading role in designing fast real-time alignment on heterogeneous hardware.
 
In recent years, ML algorithms have led to significant improvements in data processing in the field of particle physics. With latest embedded hardware, it was possible to apply those in data acquisition chains with high data throughput and low latency. E.g. live-tracking or anomaly triggering has been realised on FPGA. Several vendors are providing heterogenous hardware platforms including classic FPGA fabric, CPUs and dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) cores, allowing to embed AI close to the sensor and power-efficient data processing.
 
The LHCb group at the Physics Institute of the University of Freiburg, led by Prof. Dr. Gersabeck, covers a broad range of activities from flavour physics analyses over LHCb detector operation to the development and construction of detector components for the LHCb Upgrade II.
 
LHCb, one of CERN’s LHC experiments, has established itself over the past decade as the world’s foremost flavour factory. It has unique access to all types of heavy flavour hadrons and the ability to perform precision measurements on their decay products. The recently upgraded experiment pushes the boundary both in terms of detector technology and analysis capability. It is the first major collider experiment exploiting a full software trigger and real-time analysis system. The ultimate flavour frontier is targeted with LHCb Upgrade II, which is being developed to accumulate a total dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 300 fb-1, thus ensuring the full exploitation of the HL-LHC also in the flavour sector.
 
Prof. Dr. Gersabeck’s group is involved both in analysis and detector development work. At this intersection, it is leading the real-time calibration at LHCb, which is an integral part of first high-level software trigger (HLT1) and enables real-time analysis (RTA).
As part of the ErUM-Data consortium DEEP, the group will prototype novel algorithms for aligning the LHCb tracking system and implement them on heterogeneous hardware. This includes latest generations of FPGA-like devices as the System-on-a-Chip (SoC) AMD Versal architecture and its Coarse Grain Reconfigurable Architecture e.g. dedicated AI cores, as well as components of another consortium partner from industry. Such prototypes will be compared to existing system and other developments within LHCb.
We will further explore ML approaches both for detecting and correcting misalignments in real-time processing. The goal is to improve the sensitivity to misalignments that are hard to detect with the current approach and to increase the frequency with which misalignment can be corrected for.
The consortium DEEP aims at simplifying the application of ML algorithms on embedded processors. As a common project it will develop a transpiler toolchain based on ONNX and MLIR targeted at AMD Versal and ML SoCs of another industrial partner, to which the Freiburg group also contributes.
 
Your role includes that:
•     You take the main role to implement the prototype system
•     You contribute to the common goals of the ErUM-Data consortium DEEP, which are tools to simplify the implementation of ML algorithms on heterogeneous platforms
•     You implement algebraic algorithms on AMD Versal and other System-on-a-Chip devices
•     You develop novel algorithms for detector alignment
•     You investigate ML-based approaches to improve real-time alignment
•     You liaise with colleagues within the University and others at collaborating institutes
•     You participate in the supervision of undergraduate and postgraduate students,
•     You present the group’s findings at collaboration meetings, workshops and conferences,
•     You document the group’s findings in technical notes and journal publications,
 
You are expected:
•     To have a PhD in particle physics or equivalent qualification*,
•     To have experience in ML hardware acceleration platforms, in particular for FPGA or SoC,
•     To have experience with hardware description language and programming tool chains,
•     To have experience in ML model development and software programming,
•     To be able to communicate to a wide range of audiences and have a strong track record of presentations and publications
•     To have experience in the supervision of undergraduate and postgraduate students,
•     To be able to execute projects and to document their progress,
•     To be willing to travel as required, and
•     To be willing to engage in professional development as required.
 
*Applications from related fields such as informatics, electrical or software engineering are welcome, given qualification and the willingness to familiarise with the particle physics landscape and requirements.
 
You can expect:
•     Support by experienced group members and collaborators within the consortium,
•     Work with an industrial partner from the field of SoC for ML applications,
•     Flexible work time models,
•     Attractive sports opportunities and after-work activities,
•     A group that values equity of access and diversity in an open, friendly and social working atmosphere,
•     Reduced-price public transport passes (Jobticket BW or Deutschlandticket), and

The position is fixed-term until 31.10.2028 (§ 2 Abs. 2 WissZeitVG) with the possibility of extension. The salary will be determined in accordance with E13 TV-L.

The Laboratoire Leprince-Ringuet (LLR) is inviting applications for a two-years postdoctoral position within the CMS group, in the context of the “DRIFTS” project funded by the ANR.
The LLR is a laboratory of the CNRS/IN2P3 and the École Polytechnique, one of the grandes écoles of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IPP) specialized in science and engineering. The LLR is dedicated to fundamental research in high-energy particle physics and astroparticle physics. Its members work on the LHCb and CMS experiments at the LHC, the T2K, Super-K and Hyper-K neutrino experiments in Japan, and in FERMI, HESS and CTA for gamma-ray astronomy. 
The CMS group of LLR is a founding member of the CMS Collaboration and is composed of about 30 members. It has designed, built, and is responsible for the operation of the Level-1 (L1) trigger for the electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL). It has also designed the calorimeter mechanics and contributed to the front-end readout electronics. It has major involvement in particle reconstruction and identification with the e/gamma and tau Physics Object Groups, and contributed to the development of the Particle Flow event reconstruction. It is among the leading protagonists within the CMS Collaboration in electroweak (di-bosons, triple gauge couplings, etc.), heavy ions, and Higgs physics. 
The group is also strongly involved in the development of the future high-granularity endcap calorimeter (HGCAL) for the high-luminosity phase of the LHC, in particular on its mechanical design, on the generation of the L1 trigger primitives, and on the development of offline reconstruction algorithms. In addition, it is participating in the assembly of the detector at CERN. DRIFTS is a collaborative project between CEA/IRFU, CERN and LLR. It aims to demonstrate novel real-time trigger reconstruction architectures for future particle collider experiments, based on deep learning models distributed across multiple hardware processing stages. The HGCAL will serve as a platform to evaluate these developments using existing hardware components.
The successful candidate will contribute to the simulation of a high-granular calorimeter with Geant4 as well as its readout and trigger electronic chain. The candidate will also develop and optimize deep learning models, trained for the reconstruction of events generated with this simulation framework and targeting a distributed application. 
The duration of this postdoctoral position will be for up to 2 years, and is expected to start at the beginning of January 2026, with possibility to start at a later date. The position will be based at the LLR in Palaiseau (near Paris) with close collaboration with colleagues from CEA/IRFU and from CERN. Travels to CERN are expected as needed. For questions about the position, please contact Jean-Baptiste Sauvan (jean-baptiste.sauvan@cern.ch)

Eligibility criteria

  • Experience in training and using Machine Learning models is desired

  • Experience with FPGA firmware development and familiarity with trigger systems would be beneficial

jobs.title: Exploring the Quantum Universe: PhD Opportunities in Quantum Technologies for Fundamental Physics
jobs.description:
We invite applications for three fully funded home or international PhD positions in Quantum Technologies for Fundamental Physics at the University of Manchester. The successful candidates will join Prof. Silke Weinfurtner’s research group, the Gravity Laboratory, within the Photon Science Institute and the Centre for Quantum Science and Engineering. You’ll become part of a dynamic, interdisciplinary team working at the intersection of quantum fluids, quantum technology, and quantum field theory.

Manchester has made significant new investments in quantum research, creating one of the most vibrant environments in the UK for quantum science and technology. As part of the Department of Physics and Astronomy, you’ll benefit from world-class facilities, cross-disciplinary collaborations, and training in cutting-edge experimental methods, theoretical frameworks, and data-analysis tools.

About the research

The group develops synthetic quantum systems — laboratory setups that mimic phenomena from high-energy physics and gravity. These quantum simulators let us study how quantum fields behave near black holes and in the early universe, recreating processes of particle creation in curved spacetime that are otherwise impossible to observe directly.

We focus on quantum liquids, especially superfluid helium-4, where quantum coherence extends across macroscopic scales. In this extraordinary medium, waves and vortices become quantised, giving rise to phenomena that have no classical analogue. Superfluid helium supports a rich spectrum of bulk and surface excitations, and in the form of ultrathin films — only hundreds of nanometres thick — it exhibits “third sound,” a collective oscillation unique to two-dimensional quantum systems. These remarkable properties make superfluid helium an ideal platform for exploring quantum phenomena and for developing new quantum technologies.

The Gravity Laboratory takes a unique threefold approach, combining experimental versatility, theoretical innovation, and creative collaboration. We operate both classical and quantum fluid laboratories, allowing for rapid prototyping in classical systems and exploration of quantum phenomena in superfluid environments. In parallel, we integrate theory and experiment, working with leading theorists to develop new frameworks and high-level modelling for synthetic quantum systems. We also collaborate with established artists, co-creating artworks and scientific projects that expand how we think about and conduct research.

If you’re fascinated by modern physics, from quantum field theory, particle physics, and general relativity to the emerging areas of quantum technologies, or enjoy more hands-on topics like fluids, superfluidity, and precision optics, you’ll find this research especially rewarding.

PhD opportunities and training

Depending on your background and interests, projects can emphasize experiment, theory, or a mix of both — but all involve a strong hands-on component. We are looking for students who are curious, creative, and eager to learn across traditional boundaries. Whether you enjoy building instruments, developing theoretical models, or connecting theory to experiment, you’ll find an environment that encourages exploration and initiative.

As a PhD student in the Gravity Laboratory, you will develop an exceptionally broad and versatile skill set. You’ll gain experience in cryogenics, vacuum and gas-handling systems, low-noise electronics, and optical instrumentation, as well as in precision measurement and high-resolution imaging techniques. Alongside this experimental training, you’ll learn to apply and develop quantum field theory methods and information-theoretic tools to interpret experimental results and design new synthetic quantum systems. These transferable skills are highly valued across research, technology, and data-driven industries.

Your PhD project will be shaped around your interests and can evolve as you grow scientifically. Possible directions span the development of synthetic quantum systems that model extreme phenomena such as black holes and the early universe, the creation of novel quantum devices and imaging techniques using superfluid helium, and the engineering of ultra-stable cryogenic environments for precision experiments. Alongside these efforts, you may apply quantum field theory and information-theoretic tools to link experiment and theory. Several concrete projects are available and will be matched to each student’s background and interests, with all researchers working closely within the collaborative Gravity Laboratory team.

Supervisory team: Prof. Silke Weinfurtner (Primary Supervisor), Gravity Laboratory, Photon Science Institute & Centre for Quantum Science and Engineering, University of Manchester

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Position in GPU-Accelerated Simulation for the JUNO Neutrino Experiment

The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is poised
to deliver groundbreaking insights into neutrino physics with its unprecedented scale: 
a 20-kiloton liquid scintillator detector instrumented with over 40,000
photomultiplier tubes (PMTs), making it the world's largest scintillator-based
experiment. As JUNO proceeds with it's early data-taking phase, the
computational demands are immense and growing. Cosmic muons traversing the massive,
high-yield scintillator volume generate many millions of optical photons per event,
creating severe bottlenecks in simulation, calibration, reconstruction,
analysis, and visualization. Traditional CPU-based approaches, reliant on
serial processing, are increasingly untenable as experimental data volumes
explode and Moore's Law plateaus, rendering conventional computing models
economically unsustainable.

To meet these challenges, JUNO is embracing GPU acceleration.
Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) unlock parallel processing at scales unattainable 
elsewhere, delivering performance gains of several orders-of-magnitude, but only if 
algorithms, data structures, and workflows are fundamentally reorganized for GPU-native execution. 
This requires deep expertise in bridging high-energy physics simulations with modern
high-performance computing (HPC) techniques, ensuring seamless integration
across the full data processing pipeline.

We seek a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to spearhead advancements in
GPU-accelerated optical photon simulation for JUNO, with a principal focus on
the Opticks package. Opticks is an open-source project that implements 
optical photon simulation using GPU accelerated ray tracing from NVIDIA OptiX,  
and integrates this with the Geant4 Monte Carlo simulation. By offloading photon
propagation to the GPU Opticks achieves dramatic speedups that can exceed 100x 
over CPU equivalents for complex detector geometries. 
However, realizing this potential demands meticulous maintenance of GPU-optimized 
detector models and rigorous validation against experimental data.

In this role, you will:

- Collaborate directly with Simon Blyth, the creator and lead maintainer of
 Opticks, to enhance core capabilities of the package. 
 This can include everything from fundamental improvements to the Opticks geometry model
 and the translation of Geant4 geometries through to extending integration with Geant4.
 Examples of possible tasks include:

 * implementing alternative CSG intersection algorithms, that would be adopted if 
  performance or robustness benefits are demonstrated
 * tuning server/client Opticks to maximize GPU utilization for production 
 * add multi-threading and multi-GPU processing support
 * expand Opticks to profit from non-NVIDIA GPUs, potentially requiring 
  first principal development of ray trace acceleration structures

- Maintain the automated translation of the evolving JUNO detector geometry
 to a GPU native form, requiring detailed knowledge of the Geant4 and Opticks geometry models.  

- Enhance ray traced and rasterized visualization of detector geometry together with simulated
 event representations. Adding VR/AR device support is also possible, enabling immersive 
 experiences from inside the simulation.

- Integrate and benchmark Opticks within the JUNO simulation workflow, focusing
 on automated validation of the Opticks simulation.

- Extend GPU acceleration beyond simulation to other JUNO data processing
 domains such as reconstruction and calibration.

- Contribute to the broader Opticks community through code releases,
 documentation, and workshops, fostering adoption in other experiments
 such as future neutrino or dark matter detectors.

This position offers a unique opportunity to make tangible, high-impact
contributions at the intersection of particle physics and computational
science. The scale of JUNO amplifies the stakes: your innovations will directly
enable the production of large simulated event samples that are essential for 
improving understanding of the JUNO detector. 

The role is embedded within the JUNO international collaboration, 
providing access to world-class facilities, including GPU workstations and clusters 
and opportunities for travel to experiments and conferences.

Ideal candidates will hold a PhD in Physics, Computer Science, or a related field
and demonstrate an aptitude and willingness to learn new tools, innovate and 
act independently. Candidates are expected to have demonstrated expertise 
spanning the majority of the below areas:

- Geant4 based detector simulation, particularly optical processes and geometry

- Familiarity with neutrino experiments and large-scale HEP data processing

- GPU computation development with CUDA, Thrust, OptiX, PyTorch : optimization experience is particularly useful

- GPU visualization with OpenGL or Vulkan, also experience with Unity or Unreal is beneficial

- Software development and debugging in both C++ and Python, familiarity with gdb, git

We value candidates who thrive in interdisciplinary teams, possess strong
problem-solving skills, and are passionate about pushing the boundaries of
simulation fidelity and efficiency. This is a full-time, fixed-term appointment
(initially 2 years, renewable based on performance and funding), with a
competitive salary and benefits package commensurate with experience. The
position is based at the Institute of High Energy Physics, Beijing, China.

To apply, please submit a cover letter (2 pages max), CV, and three letters of
reference to Prof. Ziyan Deng via email to dengzy@ihep.ac.cn 
Applications received by January 7, 2026 will receive full consideration. For
inquiries, also contact Prof. Ziyan Deng 

Join us in harnessing GPU power to illuminate the neutrino while shaping the 
future of computational particle physics.

jobs.title: PhD studentship: Tabletop levitating quantum sensors for dark matter detection
jobs.description:
This PhD project will develop a new tabletop experiment using levitated quantum sensor technology. In these devices, tiny silica nanoparticles are suspended in vacuum using focused laser beams (“optical tweezers”). When cooled and controlled to the standard quantum limit (SQL), these nanoparticles act as ultra-sensitive mechanical oscillators. Passing dark matter particles, new otherwise-invisible particles, or quantum gravity forces can impart tiny forces on the trapped nanoparticles, causing minute displacements in their motion.

Measuring these effects through a range of techniques offers a new route to detecting these phenomena, well beyond the reach of current approaches. The project will build on recent breakthroughs in Manchester in quantum engineering and particle physics. You will work as part of a new interdisciplinary collaboration between the Quantum Engineering Lab (Electrical Engineering) and the Dark Matter Detection Research Group (Physics), based in the Photon Science Institute, University of Manchester.

Together, these teams are currently developing novel experimental setups to trap an array of levitated nanoparticles operating at or beyond the SQL. By scaling up from a single nanoparticle to arrays, and exploiting collective quantum effects such as synchronisation and correlations, the experiment could achieve sensitivity not just to the presence of dark matter, but also other key features and properties of unknown and unexpected phenomena.

You will be jointly supervised by Prof. Darren Price (Physics) and Dr. Jayadev Vijayan (Electrical Engineering), gaining experience and opportunities across both disciplines. You will work closely with postdoctoral researchers, engineers, and PhD peers, and engage with international collaborations in dark matter and quantum sensing.

This project offers the opportunity to make cutting-edge developments in levitated nanoparticle arrays for dark matter detection and other fundamental physics phenomena. It will place you at the interface of particle physics and quantum technology, preparing you for a research career at the forefront of discovery science or for application of these skills to other sectors.

Further details: https://www.findaphd.com/phds/project/fse-bicentenary-phd-developing-tabletop-levitating-quantum-sensors-to-detect-dark-matter-and-other-fundamental-interactions/?p188745

If you don’t already have an applicant account, please follow the instructions here.
When applying, you’ll need to specify the full name of this project "Developing tabletop levitating quantum sensors to detect dark matter and other fundamental interactions", the supervisor name (Prof. Darren Price), details of your previous study, and names and contact details of two referees. You also need to provide a Personal Statement describing the motivation to apply to the project and your CV. Your application cannot be processed without all of the required documents, and we cannot accept responsibility for late or missed deadlines where applications are incomplete.

Equality, diversity and inclusion are fundamental to the success of The University of Manchester, and are at the heart of all of our activities. jobs.title: Post-doc for ultracold neutron science and applications
jobs.description:
Neutrons make up 50% of matter on earth, but remain one of its most mysterious components: their decay lifetime is less well-known than the age of the Universe, and their internal charge structure is deeply connected to the absence of antimatter in the cosmos.

The new ultracold neutron source SuperSUN was recently brought into service at the Insitut Laue-Langevin, and now delivers storable neutrons with unprecedented high number densities. Its main user experiment, PanEDM, seeks to measure the neutron's the neutron's permanent electric dipole moment and additionally paves the way for in-situ experiments with much higher statistical sensitivity. Emerging applications, such as storage of gravitationally-bound quantum states for spectroscopy and quantum computation, broaden the general science case for helium-based sources of ultracold neutrons. All other operating sources deliver much higher-energy ultracold neutrons, raising both new technical challenges and unique opportunities for novel experiments over the next years at SuperSUN.

The successful candidate will develop and bring into service new neutron-optical elements, exploiting them for science with the immediate aim to measure and efficiently deliver SuperSUN's characteristic low-energy ultracold neutron spectrum for external experiments. Development work is based at Heidelberg University, and locally supported by engineering design staff and an extensive mechanical workshop. Extensive participation on-site at the Insitut Laue-Langevin, for preparing and carrying out beamtime measurements, is also expected.

Required qualifications:
  • PhD or equivalent degree in experimental physics, or a closely related field
  • Practical experience with experimental hardware, data-taking, and analysis
Desired qualifications:
  • Experience with ultracold neutron experiments
  • Experience mentoring (or co-mentoring) PhD projects, or Bachelor/Master students
  • Strong background in mathematics, simulations, or signal processing
  • Strong writing skills for scientific English
While service duties are not a formal obligation of the position, teaching and outreach opportunities are available.

Applications will be evaluated on an ongoing basis, until the position is filled.

The Neutrino and Rare Events Group at Columbia University is looking for excellent candidates for an open Postdoctoral Research Associate position. The group's research efforts are focused on searches for new physics and astrophysical observations with current and future experiments that make use of liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs)—a high-resolution imaging technology for particle detection. The efforts include physics analysis as well as hardware R&D particularly in the area of LArTPC readout electronics, pixelated readout, and data acquisition systems, and build on the group’s leading involvement in past and current LArTPC experiments including MicroBooNE, SBND, and DUNE. 

The position offers opportunities for involvement in the Gamma-Ray and AntiMatter Survey (GRAMS) project. GRAMS is a NASA-selected "Physics of the Cosmos” mission, that aims to utilize a balloon- (and, ultimately, satellite-) borne LArTPC to deliver astrophysical MeV gamma-ray observations and indirect dark matter searches with significantly improved sensitivity over current/planned instruments. The project is currently funded to demonstrate LArTPC performance during a prototype balloon flight (“pGRAMS”) planned for spring 2026. The Neutrinos and Rare Events group at Columbia is responsible for the readout and data acquisition (DAQ) system of pGRAMS, pGRAMS simulation and data analysis, as well as physics sensitivity and LArTPC readout/DAQ design studies for future GRAMS science flights. 

An ideal candidate for this position will be expected to take a leading role in the upcoming pGRAMS flight commissioning, operation, simulation, and data analysis, including the development of new reconstruction and software tools for the data processing and analysis pipelines. An ideal candidate would also work with other physicists, electronics engineers and/or computer scientists to develop new readout or data-processing hardware technologies and real-time AI methodologies for LArTPCs, and carry out demonstrations with dedicated teststands.

A PhD in physics, astrophysics, or similar field is required, with a strong background in data analysis, reconstruction, and/or simulations. A strong background in LArTPC DAQ systems is strongly preferred. Experience with scientific software development, online software workflows, and/or machine learning/AI is advantageous. jobs.title: Two PhD positions in the ATLAS group
jobs.description:
The organization
Nikhef is the national institute for subatomic physics in the Netherlands. At Nikhef, approximately 220 physicists and 80 technical staff work together in an open and international scientific environment. Together they perform theoretical and experimental research in the fields of particle and astroparticle physics. Nikhef is a partnership between six major Dutch universities and NWO-I Foundation, the Institutes Organization of the Dutch Research Council (NWO).

Among the research collaborations Nikhef participates in are the ALICE, ATLAS and LHCb experiments at CERN, the KM3NeT neutrino telescope in the Mediterranean, the Virgo gravitational waves interferometer in Pisa, the Xenon-nT dark matter experiment in Gran Sasso, the Pierre Auger cosmic ray observatory in Argentina, and the eEDM research programme in Groningen. There are also scientific groups on Theory, Physics Data Processing and Detector R&D. Nikhef avails over excellently equipped technical departments in mechanics, electronics and computing.

The Nikhef ATLAS group
The Nikhef ATLAS group consists of a total of 15 scientific staff, typically 5 postdocs and 15 PhD students. As a founding member of the ATLAS collaboration, the group has a long-term involvement in detector construction (the semiconductor tracker, barrel muon chambers, readout, alignment, and data acquisition).

For the phase-2 upgrade (2027-2030), we will instrument and commission one of the end-caps of a new all-silicon inner tracking system (ITk) in Amsterdam, commission the High Granularity Timing Detector (HGTD), and develop the new universal readout system (FELIX) for ATLAS detector systems.

The group also has a strong record in track reconstruction, flavour tagging algorithm development as well as physics data analysis, with a focus on Higgs boson physics, top quark physics, and searches for new physics signatures.

The positions
After the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012, one of the crucial future challenges for the LHC is to probe its most enigmatic property, the Higgs potential, which can manifest itself in LHC collisions through the production of Higgs boson pairs. These decays, which are 1000 times more rare than single Higgs production according to the Standard Model have not yet been observed. Observation of two-Higgs production is one the most important milestone for the LHC physics program, and will help constrain our knowledge of the Higgs potential, which has shaped the universe at its time of creation, and may hold strong clues about the existence of new physics beyond the Standard Model. 

Position 1 will focus on the search for the extremely rare process of ttHH production in LHC Run-3 data. This search will include all tt final states, and will include boosted final states. The analysis strategy is strongly focused on advanced machine learning techniques, developing attention-based transformer models that will directly classify events from the low-level data, rather than high-level objects, and which may ultimately include higher-level tasks such as Higgs boson mass regression for the analyzed data. The boosted object analysis will have a strong synergy with boosted analyses we are performing in other two-Higgs channels. This position is co-supervised by prof. dr. Ivo van Vulpen, dr. Clara Nellist, and dr. Sascha Caron. The candidates is employed by the University of Amsterdam, is primarily based at Nikhef in Amsterdam.

Position 2 will focus on the reconstruction of two-Higgs decay channel into a pair of photons and a pair of b-quarks (HH->bbγγ) , which currently provides the tightest constraints, and on the combined interpretation of all reconstructed diHiggs channels. Apart from the Run-3 diHiggs combination of all channels, which will provide the ultimate statement on diHiggs production that can be obtained with the LHC Run-3 data, a combination of single-Higgs, di-Higgs and triple-Higgs production measurements will allow to constrain the trilinear and quartic Higgs coupling, and thus the shape of the Higgs potential with unprecedented precision. In this position you will closely work together with PhD students involved in the main diHiggs channels (bbbb, bbττ and bbVV) for the combined interpretation and with a postdoc that is being recruited simultaneously that work on novel ML-based strategies to improve the precision of diHiggs combined interpretations. This position is co-supervised by prof. dr. Wouter Verkerke, prof. dr. Tristan du Pree. The candidates is employed by the University of Amsterdam, is primarily based at Nikhef in Amsterdam.

The positions offered here are part of a NWO-funded physics program “The potential of the Higgs boson”, with prof. dr. Pamela Ferrari as principle investigator, which will ultimately comprise 7 PhD positions and 2 postdoc positions in the Nikhef ATLAS group in the period 2025-2030 all focused on the Higgs boson potential, complemented by 9 Nikhef staff scientists that offer supervision, networking opportunities and a specialized training program in data analysis techniques and Higgs boson physics.

Requirements
We are looking for PhD candidates with an (almost) completed Master degree in high-energy physics or in a closely related field. The ideal candidate has a strong interest in data analysis, has good software skills (Python, C++, ROOT) and has (some) research experience in experimental particle physics. Experience with machine learning algorithms and software is desirable but not required.

Offer
A temporary fulltime contract for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. During the doctoral program there is the possibility for extended stays at CERN, up to a total of 1 year. 

You will be employed at the University of Amsterdam, depending on the position. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between €3,059 and €3,881 (scale P). The salary is based on a full-time contract. On top of the monthly salary, excellent secondary benefits apply, such as a 8% holiday allowance in May, and a 8.3% year-end allowance in December and an excellent pension plan. Further details can be found here,.

Application
Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply by filling in the application form. The deadline for applications is Nov 16th, 2025. Please be prepared to upload a short cover letter, a curriculum vitae and have the email address of at least two referees ready who are willing to send a letter of recommendation on your behalf. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure.

Please indicate in which position(s) you are interested in your cover letter. Interviews with selected candidates are foreseen in the period of Dec 8-16. For further information, feel free to contact list co-supervisors for details on the positions, or prof. dr. Wouter Verkerke for general information about the Nikhef ATLAS group.

About the University of Amsterdam
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The Institute of Physics (IoP) is located in the centre of the Amsterdam Science Park. The IoP – as part of the Faculty of Science – is housed in a modern building with excellent labs and technical facilities. Surrounded by several national research institutes and with our partners at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, the institute is part of a strong physics centre of international standing. One of the institutes that the IoP has very close ties to is Nikhef, the national institute for subatomic physics in The Netherlands.
